members.reason: Three independent provisions: cancellation of section 55 on signing; replacement of calendar year by fiscal year beginning July 1 in section 524 effective January 1, 1932; special accounting rule for January 1-June 30, 1932. The temporary rule does not sunset the other provisions. No whole-order first end established. The temporary accounting applicability period closes after June 30, 1932, but actual settlement or continuing liability is not proved.

Five modifications: item 8 passport issue $9 and renewal $5; delete form references 37, 38, 39 from items 24, 25, 26; rewrite item 47 no-fee certificates to require written Secretary of State orders for export trade. No first end established. Neither item 8 passport renewal wording nor the act of text amendment is an own-term sunset. EO7968 is later direct supersession, not proof of first cessation.

Original page 72 authorizes a personal civil-service exception for Dorothy I. Sinnott. EO6179A paragraph (6) identifies her appointment May 13, 1931, and the actor revokes the listed appointment June 16, 1933. This supports an actual-appointment lead earlier than revocation, but does not expressly say whether the exemption was exhausted at appointment or persisted as her legal status. Do not substitute June 16 for first cessation without resolving that issue.

OFR images confirm continuing Balboa and Cristobal division boundaries effective 1931-09-02. EO 5880 adds territory rather than wholly ending these boundaries. EO 7676 sections 13-14 give a candidate supersession on 1937-08-25, but actor raw custody and earlier-end/savings closure are missing.

Two parent scopes: Consular Regulations section 544 and Instructions to Diplomatic Officers chapter XX section 11. Recurring postage voucher, official-use, and strict-account requirements; no own sunset. No first end established. EO7968 is a later direct supersession candidate and cancels chapter XX of Part I, but parent/version reconciliation remains open.

One operative no-fee tariff item 47; lead merely introduces it. Government-issued origin/manufacture/inspection certificate copies required for advancing export trade. No first end established. Reject May 16, 1932 as an automatic end: the clause continues amended under the owner ruling. EO7968 remains a later supersession candidate.

OFR images establish section I boundary addition, section II construction-period cession description, and section III force only while United States exercises jurisdiction. Neither construction completion nor jurisdiction cessation is established by this packet. Machine own_terms is empty despite the express contingent end.

Official page 512 authorizes appointment of Lamar Costello as Supervisor of Detentions, $3,000 annually, Immigration Service at Ellis Island, without civil-service requirements. EO6179A paragraph (5) records his August 1, 1932 appointment and revokes the appointment June 16, 1933. Actual appointment precedes revocation; no exact first ending is submitted until consumption of permission versus continuing exemption is resolved.

OFR 1974 Hoover vol. II printed pp. 1286-87, PDF pp. 515-16: one temporary Acker exemption until November 1, 1932. EO 5940 printed p. 1322, PDF p. 551 cites and further exempts Acker before that date, without a new endpoint. The first end cannot be assigned to November 1.

Three tariff changes: item 1 substitutes original for duplicate; item 9 adds existing item 10 provisions and states Chinese passport/certificate visa $9 with exceptions for a,b,c above; item 10 replaced by affidavit-of-identity visa $9. The scan resolves the OCR-displaced fee columns. No first end established. These are continuing tariff amendments rather than performed one-time services. EO7968 gives a later supersession candidate only.

OFR image confirms a personal exemption from section 204 of the 1932 Act with no express end. June 30 1933 occurs only in the appropriation-act title and is not an operative sunset. First cessation and residual rights need statute and person-specific evidence.

Actual pages 528-529 grant John P. McDowell exemption from section 204 Part II of the June 30, 1932 act. There is no express duration or sunset. June 30, 1933 appears only in the cited act title. No held ending instrument or personnel event dates the end of this exemption, and a current predicate through cutoff is not established.

Actual PDF532 grants Albert D. Davis, cabinet maker at United States Shipping Board, exemption from section 204 Part II of June 30, 1932 act. It contains no own sunset. Fiscal year ending June 30, 1933 is part of statutory title only. No held dated first-ending source or current predicate closes lifecycle.

OFR image confirms continuing authorization to test congressional nominees. EO 12553 text explicitly lists EO 5918 for revocation, a 1986-02-25 candidate, but the actor raw PDF is not held and earlier statutory or agency changes and savings remain open.

OFR images confirm discretionary reemployment-priority rulemaking plus supersession of five earlier instruments. EO 8973 recognizes the list in 1941 without revoking it. EO 9830 Part III expressly revokes EO 5924 under an order-wide May 1 1947 effective clause; earliest-ending and residual-rights closure still lacking.

OFR 1974 Hoover vol. II printed p. 1322, PDF p. 551: one exemption of Acker, with no until date. The recital of prior exemptions and the statute title's fiscal year do not terminate the new exemption.
OFR 1974 Hoover vol. II printed pp. 1341-42, PDF pp. 570-71: one exemption of George R. Wales, with no until date. Both original pages and the closing No. 5951 line were checked.
OFR 1974 Hoover vol. II printed p. 1404, PDF p. 633: one exemption of Oliver M. Maxam, with no until date; following EO 6005 is separate.
